page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.3xlarge is a storage-focused instance built on KVM virtualization and the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz, providing 6 physical cores and 12 virtual CPUs via hyperthreading. The hardware configuration features 48 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per physical core, accompanied by 33 MB of L3 cache. Storage is a defining feature, bundling 35,433 GB of local mechanical HDD storage directly attached to the instance. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmarks reflect a distinction between single-threaded and multi-threaded CPU capabilities. Single-core tests such as stress-ng single-core (1102.49) and Geekbench single-core (911.0) fall into lower performance tiers, and single-threaded gzip compression demonstrates low processing throughput at 18.96 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core performance achieves average results, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 4584.0, a multi-core stress-ng rating of 8789.97, and a PassMark CPU score of 10074.03. Memory read bandwidth reaches 54.9 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, while Redis SET operations handle 8.27 million operations per second.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the primary trade-off of the ecs.d1.3xlarge centers on dense local magnetic disk storage balanced against legacy single-thread processor efficiency. While the older Intel Xeon v4 architecture lacks high single-core IPC, it delivers high cost efficiency per gigabyte of local storage capacity. This profile makes the instance suitable for large-scale data storage, distributed file systems, batch log processing, and relational or non-relational database workloads requiring extensive bulk storage rather than intense single-thread computational performance.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.3xlarge is a local storage instance optimized for high-capacity data retention and sequential throughput. Running on KVM virtualization, it features an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 CPU operating at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, delivering 6 physical cores and 12 vCPUs. The setup is equipped with 48 GB of memory, a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps, and a bundled local HDD storage capacity of 35,433 GB. Benchmark results indicate low single-core processing capabilities, balanced by average multi-core CPU metrics, including a PassMark CPU score of 10074.03 and a multi-threaded stress-ng result of 8789.97. Memory throughput reaches 54.9 GB/sec for uncached read operations. The instance offers strong cost efficiency for bulk storage workloads, trading peak per-core processing speed for high local disk density. It is suited for big data storage, log processing, and distributed database nodes.
